title: Styling Vue Components
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of Styling Vue Components in a Vue 3 application.
Apply at least one of the syllabus subtopics in a small, inspectable example.
Verify one expected behavior and identify a relevant edge case.

content.intro: This lesson studies Styling Vue Components within Styling, Transitions, and Animations. The source PDF subtopics are preserved below and connected to an original working-style example.
content.why_it_matters: Useful motion and visual feedback should clarify state changes without reducing readability or accessibility.

content_blocks.title: Styling Vue Components: Component communication
content_blocks.alt_text: Component communication diagram for lesson 61: Styling Vue Components. Parent owns the value or business intent → Child receives data and renders its view → Child emits intent; parent decides updates
content_blocks.caption: Component flow: data moves into children through props; emitted events communicate requested changes back to the owner.

content_blocks.title: The idea in context
content_blocks.text: Vue styling combines global CSS, scoped SFC styles, dynamic style/class bindings, and state-driven transitions. This lesson focuses on Styling Vue Components. Start by naming the state, component, browser behavior, or deployment boundary involved; then predict what should change and test the smallest example.

items.title: Global CSS
items.text: For Global CSS, keep the visual rule in CSS where possible and bind reactive values only when state genuinely changes presentation. Check responsive behavior and reduced-motion preferences; animation should communicate state rather than block interaction.

items.title: Component-level styling
items.text: For Component-level styling, document what data enters the component, which events leave it, and where shared content or behavior belongs. Keep props one-way, emit changes rather than mutating parent-owned values, and add slots only when a real composition point is needed.

items.title: Scoped styles
items.text: For Scoped styles, keep the visual rule in CSS where possible and bind reactive values only when state genuinely changes presentation. Check responsive behavior and reduced-motion preferences; animation should communicate state rather than block interaction.

content_blocks.expected_output: Toggling the button fades the paragraph in or out.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run as App.vue; verify behavior with reduced motion and do not rely on animation to communicate the only status cue.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the initial values or original code, reload the development app/test, and repeat once with a boundary or failure case. Remove temporary logs and test data before committing.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Work through Styling Vue Components with a predict–change–verify loop. First state the expected UI or console output. Change only the relevant input/state value, then observe the result. Compare it with the expected output in the code block; if it differs, check the exact file, runtime/version, browser Console, and network response before widening the investigation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Extend the example to include “Component-level styling”. Keep the same behavior for the ordinary input, then try an empty, invalid, repeated, or failure condition that makes sense for the example. Record the expected result before testing.

items.title: Assuming behavior instead of checking it
items.text: Write down the expected result and reproduce the issue in the smallest possible example; inspect the browser Console and the exact reactive value or request.

items.title: Ignoring an edge case
items.text: Try empty input, a missing item, repeated interaction, a failed request, or unmounting while work is pending; handle the case explicitly.

items.title: Putting every responsibility in one component
items.text: Separate display, reusable logic, API service, and shared state when that boundary makes the behavior easier to test and explain.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember: Vue styling combines global CSS, scoped SFC styles, dynamic style/class bindings, and state-driven transitions. For Styling Vue Components, keep the example small, verify the rendered or logged result, and consult the official references when behavior depends on a specific Vue or ecosystem version.

content_blocks.title: Accessibility, version, and runtime notes
content_blocks.text: Use semantic HTML, readable labels, keyboard-operable controls, and visible errors where the example interacts with users. Vue examples are intended for Vue 3.x with create-vue/Vite unless a legacy or specialist lesson explicitly says otherwise. This CodeLeaf playground does not execute arbitrary Vue code; the snippets are labeled for static validation and should be run in a separate local project.

content.task: Create a small example for “Styling Vue Components” that applies “Global CSS”, predicts the expected result, and verifies a relevant boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the named Vue concept rather than only mentioning it.
The expected output or observable behavior is written down and can be checked locally.
At least one boundary, loading, invalid-input, or failure case is tested or explicitly reasoned about.
The example uses semantic/accessible interaction patterns and does not treat frontend state as authoritative security.
hints: Start with the smallest observable part of “Global CSS”.
Predict the output before changing one input at a time.
Use the browser Console, Vue DevTools, or the appropriate test runner to isolate a mismatch.

common_mistakes.problem: The example only covers the happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Real interfaces receive empty values, delayed responses, invalid input, and failed requests.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one realistic edge/failure case and state its expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: The code assumes an API or feature exists in every runtime.
common_mistakes.why: Tool and API support depends on Vue, the build tool, or the chosen SSR/test framework.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the linked official reference and record the runtime/version assumption.

summary: Styling Vue Components belongs to the broader area Styling, Transitions, and Animations.
The main concept to practice is Global CSS.
Verify a normal result and one meaningful boundary case before using the pattern in a production feature.
